Who Should Read This Book谁应该阅读本书

At this point, nearly every developer is a developer or consumer (or both) of distributed systems. Even relatively simple mobile applications are backed with cloud APIs so that their data can be present on whatever device the customer happens to be using. Whether you are new to developing distributed systems or an expert with scars on your hands to prove it, the patterns and components described in this book can transform your development of distributed systems from art to science. Reusable components and patterns for distributed systems will enable you to focus on the core details of your application. This book will help any developer become better, faster, and more efficient at building distributed systems.

时至今日，几乎每位开发者都是分布式系统的开发者或使用者（或二者兼具）。即便是相对简单的移动应用，其背后也有云端 API 支撑，好让用户无论用哪台设备都能看到自己的数据。无论你是分布式系统开发的新手，还是手上带着伤疤的资深专家，本书描述的模式与组件都能把你的分布式系统开发从“艺术”变为“科学”。可复用的分布式系统组件与模式，将让你专注于应用本身的核心细节。本书将帮助任何开发者在构建分布式系统时变得更好、更快、更高效。

Why I Wrote This Book我为什么写这本书

Throughout my career as a developer of a variety of software systems, from web search to the cloud, I have built a large number of scalable, reliable distributed systems. Each of these systems was, by and large, built from scratch. In general, this is true of all distributed applications. Despite having many of the same concepts and even at times nearly identical logic, the ability to apply patterns or reuse components is often very, very challenging. This forced me to waste time reimplementing systems, and each system ended up less polished than it might have otherwise been.

在我的职业生涯中，我开发过从网页搜索到云计算等各类软件系统，构建过大量可扩展、可靠的分布式系统。这些系统基本上每一个都是从零开始造的——总体而言，所有分布式应用皆是如此。尽管它们有许多相同的概念、有时甚至逻辑几乎一致，但要真正套用模式或复用组件，往往非常、非常困难。这迫使我浪费时间反复重做系统，而每个系统最终都不如本可达到的那样精致。

The recent introduction of containers and container orchestrators fundamentally changed the landscape of distributed system development. Suddenly we have an object and interface for expressing core distributed system patterns and building reusable containerized components. I wrote this book to bring together all of the practitioners of distributed systems, giving us a shared language and common standard library so that we can all build better systems more quickly.

容器与容器编排器的新近出现，从根本上改变了分布式系统开发的面貌。我们忽然有了一种对象和接口，用来表达分布式系统的核心模式、并构建可复用的容器化组件。我写这本书，是为了把所有分布式系统从业者凝聚到一起，给我们一套共同语言和通用标准库，让大家都能更快地构建更好的系统。

— PDF 第 14 页 —

The World of Distributed Systems Today当今的分布式系统世界

Once upon a time, people wrote programs that ran on one machine and were also accessed from that machine. The world has changed. Now, nearly every application is a distributed system running on multiple machines and accessed by multiple users from all over the world. Despite their prevalence, the design and development of these systems is often a black art practiced by a select group of wizards. But as with everything in technology, the world of distributed systems is advancing, regularizing, and abstracting. In this book I capture a collection of repeatable, generic patterns that can make the development of reliable distributed systems more approachable and efficient. The adoption of patterns and reusable components frees developers from reimplementing the same systems over and over again. This time is then freed to focus on building the core application itself.

曾几何时，人们编写的程序只在一台机器上运行，也只从那台机器上访问。世界已经变了：如今几乎每个应用都是运行在多台机器上、由世界各地的多位用户访问的分布式系统。尽管分布式系统已如此普遍，其设计与开发却常常仍是一小群“巫师”施展的黑魔法。但正如技术领域的一切那样，分布式系统的世界也在前进、规范化和抽象化。本书收录了一系列可复用的通用模式，让可靠分布式系统的开发变得更平易近人、也更高效。采用模式与可复用组件，能把开发者从反复重做同一套系统中解放出来，省下的时间便可专注于构建应用本身。

Navigating This Book本书导航

This book is organized into five parts as follows:

本书共分为五个部分，结构如下：

Part I, “Foundational Concepts”: Chapters 1 and 2 introduce distributed systems as well as some fundamental concepts which are essential to understanding the distributed system designs described in Part II, “Single-Node Patterns”.

第一部分“基础概念”：第 1、2 章介绍分布式系统，以及一些对理解第二部分“单节点模式”中所述分布式系统设计至关重要的基础概念。

Part II, “Single-Node Patterns”: Chapters 3 through 5 discuss reusable patterns and components that occur on individual nodes within a distributed system. They cover the sidecar, adapter, and ambassador single-node patterns.

第二部分“单节点模式”：第 3 至 5 章讨论分布式系统中出现在单个节点上的可复用模式与组件，涵盖边车（sidecar）、适配器（adapter）与大使（ambassador）三种单节点模式。

Part III, “Serving Patterns”: Chapters 6 through 8 cover multinode distributed patterns for long-running serving systems like web applications. Patterns for many different types of serving systems, including basic replication, sharding, and work sharing, are discussed. Additionally, Chapters 9 and 10 discuss essential distributed concepts like functions, event-driven programming, and leader election.

第三部分“服务模式”：第 6 至 8 章涵盖面向 Web 应用这类长期运行服务系统的多节点分布式模式，讨论了多种服务系统模式，包括基础复制、分片（sharding）与工作分担。此外，第 9、10 章讨论函数、事件驱动编程与领导者选举（leader election）等必备的分布式概念。

Part IV, “Batch Computational Patterns”: Chapters 11 through 13 cover distributed system patterns for large-scale batch data processing regarding work queues, event-based processing, and coordinated workflows.

第四部分“批处理计算模式”：第 11 至 13 章涵盖面向大规模批数据处理的分布式系统模式，涉及工作队列（work queue）、基于事件的处理与协同工作流。

— PDF 第 15 页 —

Part V, “Universal Concepts”: The book concludes with several topics that are universal to all distributed systems. Chapter 14 covers logging, monitoring, and alerting for your application; Chapter 15 provides a survey of AI infrastructure; and Chapter 16 describes many common failures and design errors that occur over and over again as we build distributed systems.

第五部分“通用概念”：本书最后讨论若干对所有分布式系统都通用的主题。第 14 章介绍应用的日志、监控与告警；第 15 章综述 AI 基础设施；第 16 章则描述我们在构建分布式系统时反复出现的许多常见故障与设计错误。

If you are an experienced distributed systems engineer, you can likely skip Chapters 1 and 2, though you may want to skim them to understand how I expect these patterns to be applied and why I think the general notion of distributed system patterns is so important.

如果你是经验丰富的分布式系统工程师，大可以跳过第 1、2 章；不过你或许仍想略读一遍，以理解我期望这些模式如何被应用、以及我为何认为“分布式系统模式”这一总体概念如此重要。

You will likely find utility in the single-node patterns, as they are the most generic and most reusable patterns in the book.

你很可能会在单节点模式中发现价值，因为它们是本书中最通用、最可复用的模式。

Depending on your goals and the systems you are interested in developing, you can choose to focus on either large-scale big data patterns or patterns for long-running servers (or both). The two parts are largely independent from each other and can be read in any order.

根据你的目标以及你感兴趣开发的系统，你可以选择聚焦于大规模大数据模式，或长期运行服务器的模式（或两者兼修）。这两大部分彼此基本独立，可按任意顺序阅读。

Likewise, if you have extensive distributed system experience, you may find that some of the early patterns chapters (e.g., Part III on naming, discovery, and load balancing) are redundant with what you already know, so feel free to skim through to gain the high-level insights—but don’t forget to look at all of the pretty pictures!

同样，如果你具备丰富的分布式系统经验，可能会觉得前面某些模式章节（例如第三部分关于命名、服务发现与负载均衡的内容）与你已知的东西重复，那就尽管略读以获取高层洞见——但别忘了看看那些漂亮的图！

Part I: Foundational Concepts第一部分：基础概念

Before we get started describing distributed systems, there are motivations and concepts that form the foundation of both why and how we build distributed systems. This section covers these foundational concepts to provide a basis for the rest of the book.

在开始描述分布式系统之前，有一些动机与概念构成了我们为何、以及如何构建分布式系统的基础。本部分将介绍这些基础概念，为本书其余部分提供根基。

Distributed systems don’t exist in a vacuum. The development of such systems is based on the evolving role of both computing and online systems in business and entertainment. In particular, in the development of always-on, mission-critical systems that we rely on every day. Additionally, the development of modern distributed systems is based on the history of how such systems have been designed and built in the past. This history of both how the systems are built, and often more importantly how they have failed, has led us to the current containerized and microservice architectures that you find in this book.

分布式系统并非存在于真空中。这类系统的发展，建立于计算与在线系统在商业和娱乐中不断演变的角色之上，尤其是我们每天依赖的、永远在线的关键业务系统的发展。此外，现代分布式系统的发展还建立在此类系统过去如何被设计和构建的历史之上。这段关于系统如何被构建、以及（往往更重要的）它们如何失败的历史，把我们带到了本书所呈现的、当前的容器化与微服务架构。

Before the design of distributed systems can be described, it is necessary to have a grounding in core concepts for how server systems operate, as well as fundamental computer science concepts like locking and APIs. It is also necessary to have a grounding in basic operations for distributed systems, such as monitoring and logging. Finally, because distributed systems involve numerous interactions across many different systems and many different requests, it is necessary to have a basic understanding of statistics and how we can measure the common behavior across the system through observing multiple different requests on different machines.

在描述分布式系统的设计之前，有必要先掌握服务器系统如何运转的核心概念，以及锁、API 等基础计算机科学概念；也有必要掌握监控、日志等分布式系统的基本运维操作。最后，由于分布式系统涉及跨多个不同系统、多个不同请求的大量交互，有必要对统计学有基本理解，并懂得如何通过在不同机器上观察多个不同请求，来度量整个系统的普遍行为。

— PDF 第 20 页 —

After reading these introductory chapters, you should have the foundational grounding in the context, history, and concepts necessary to understand how the design of these systems is described. This grounding also helps explain why some of the seemingly complex aspects of the design become necessary for reliability or scale.

读完这些导论章节后，你应当对相关背景、历史与概念具备基础认识，从而理解本书如何描述这些系统的设计。这种认识也有助于解释：设计中某些看似复杂的方面，为何为了可靠性或规模而成为必需。
